evidence_records.title: Metformin treatment is associated with reduced dementia incidence in large electronic health records cohort
evidence_records.authors: Shi, Q., Liu, S., Fonseca, V. A., Krousel-Wood, M., Bazzano, L. A.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: In this longitudinal cohort of 115,845 individuals with type 2 diabetes followed for a median of 8.2 years, metformin monotherapy was associated with a 24% lower hazard of incident dementia and Alzheimer's disease (aHR 0.76, 95% CI 0.71-0.81) compared to sulfonylurea monotherapy.
evidence_records.citation: Shi, Q. et al. (2021) Lancet Healthy Longevity, 2(11):e712-e722.

evidence_records.title: Effects of Metformin on cerebral glucose metabolism in mild cognitive impairment: Phase II biomarker analysis
evidence_records.authors: Koenig, A. M., Mechanic-Hamilton, D., Xie, S. X., Combs, M. F., Cappola, A. R.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: A randomized, double-blind crossover pilot study evaluating 2000 mg/day metformin in non-diabetic individuals with amnestic MCI showed statistically significant improvements in executive memory function and preservation of fluorodeoxyglucose FDG-PET uptake in posterior cingulate cortex.
evidence_records.citation: Koenig, A. M. et al. (2022) JAMA Neurol, 79(6):592-602.

evidence_records.title: Exenatide once weekly versus placebo in Parkinson's disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
evidence_records.authors: Athauda, D., Maclagan, K., Skene, S. S., Bajwa-Joseph, M., Letchford, D.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: Patients with Parkinson's disease receiving 2 mg subcutaneous exenatide once weekly had positive, statistically significant differences in practically defined off-medication motor scores (MDS-UPDRS Part III) at 60 weeks that persisted after a 12-week washout period.

evidence_records.title: Alcohol-abuse drug disulfiram targets cancer via p97 segregase adaptor NPL4
evidence_records.authors: Skrott, Z., Mistrik, M., Andersen, K. K., Friis, S., Majera, D., Gursky, J.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: Disulfiram metabolite ditiocarb-copper complex (CuET) binds directly to NPL4 and triggers its aggregation, thereby disabling the essential p97/VCP-NPL4-UFD1 segregase complex. This selectively kills cancer cells through proteotoxic stress.

evidence_records.title: Addition of pentoxifylline to renin-angiotensin system blockers reduces eGFR decline in diabetic kidney disease (PREDIAN)
evidence_records.authors: Navarro-González, J. F., Mora-Fernández, C., Muros de Fuentes, M., Donate-Correa, J.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: The PREDIAN trial demonstrated that addition of pentoxifylline (1200 mg/day) to standard ARB therapy in patients with stage 3-4 diabetic kidney disease resulted in a smaller decrease in eGFR (-2.1 vs -6.5 mL/min per 1.73 m2, P < 0.001) and greater reduction in urinary albumin.
evidence_records.citation: Navarro-González, J. F. et al. (2015) J Am Soc Nephrol, 26(9):2201-2210.

evidence_records.title: Antithrombotic therapy in atrial fibrillation: ACCP Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence_records.authors: You, J. J., Singer, D. E., Howard, P. A., Lane, D. A., Eckman, M. H.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: Guideline consensus strongly warns against routine addition of aspirin to oral anticoagulants (warfarin or DOACs) without verified acute coronary syndrome or mechanical valve indication, citing an annualized major bleeding rate increase of 1.5% to 2.5% without stroke prevention superiority.
evidence_records.citation: You, J. J. et al. (2012) Chest, 141(2 Suppl):e531S-e575S.

evidence_records.title: Reduced effectiveness of clopidogrel (Plavix) with omeprazole: Mechanistic CYP2C19 Pharmacogenomics
evidence_records.authors: Mega, J. L., Close, S. L., Wiviott, S. D., Shen, L., Hockett, R. D.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: Omeprazole competitive inhibition of CYP2C19 significantly reduces the bioavailability of clopidogrel active thiol metabolite by 45%, leading to diminished platelet aggregation inhibition and elevated cardiovascular hazard.
evidence_records.citation: Mega, J. L. et al. (2010) N Engl J Med, 363:1909-1917.

evidence_records.title: Concurrent use of diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs, and NSAIDs and risk of acute kidney injury: Triple Whammy
evidence_records.authors: Lapi, F., Azoulay, L., Yin, H., Nessim, S. J., Suissa, S.
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: In a nested case-control study of 487,372 antihypertensive users, concurrent use of a diuretic, an ACE inhibitor or ARB, and an NSAID was associated with a 31% increased rate of acute kidney injury (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.53), with the highest risk within the first 30 days of initiation.

evidence_records.title: Metformin in Preventing Cognitive Decline in Older Adults (MAP4AD)
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: Phase II/III double-blind placebo-controlled multi-center trial evaluating whether 24-month metformin administration slows executive and episodic cognitive decline in pre-diabetic or metabolically vulnerable adults aged 65-85.

evidence_records.title: Pharmacovigilance Signal Report: Warfarin and Antiplatelet Bleeding Disproportionality
evidence_records.authors: FDA CDER Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology
evidence_records.abstract_snippet: Data mining of over 14 million post-marketing adverse event reports identified a Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) of 3.84 for serious gastrointestinal hemorrhage with concurrent aspirin and warfarin versus monotherapy cohorts.
